# 2 Kings Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 234v–235v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_014_page_001.jpg, 2KI_014_page_002.jpg, 2KI_014_page_003.jpg

---

**1** In the second year of King Jehoash of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.

**2** He was twenty-five when he took the throne and reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jehoaddin of Jerusalem.

**3** He did what was right in the LORD's eyes — though not like David. He followed the example of his father Joash.

**4** The high places, however, were not removed. The people continued sacrificing and burning incense there.

**5** Once his grip on power was secure, he executed the officials who had assassinated his father.

**6** But he did not kill their children, following the law written in the Book of Moses, where the LORD commanded: "Parents must not be put to death for their children's sins, nor children for their parents' sins. Each person must die for their own sin."

**7** He defeated ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and captured the fortress of Sela in battle, renaming it Joktheel — a name it bears to this day.

**8** Flushed with victory, Amaziah sent a challenge to King Jehoash of Israel: "Come, let us face each other in battle."

**9** Jehoash sent back this reply: "A thistle in Lebanon once sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon: 'Give your daughter in marriage to my son.' But then a wild animal came along and crushed the thistle.

**10** Yes, you've beaten Edom — and now your success has gone to your head. Enjoy your glory and stay home! Why stir up trouble that will bring you crashing down, taking all of Judah with you?"

**11** But Amaziah refused to listen. So Jehoash marched out, and the two kings met in battle at Beth-shemesh in Judah.

**12** Judah was routed by Israel. Every soldier fled for home.

**13** Jehoash captured Amaziah at Beth-shemesh, then marched on Jerusalem. He tore down a 600-foot section of Jerusalem's wall, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.

**14** He seized all the gold and silver, every article from the LORD's temple and from the royal treasury, and took hostages back to Samaria.

**15** The rest of what Jehoash accomplished, including his war against Amaziah, is recorded in the court history of the kings of Israel.

**16** Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. His son Jeroboam succeeded him.

**17** Amaziah survived Jehoash by fifteen years.

**18** The rest of Amaziah's reign is recorded in the court history of the kings of Judah.

**19** A conspiracy formed against him in Jerusalem. He fled to Lachish, but they sent men after him and killed him there.

**20** His body was brought back on horses and buried in Jerusalem, in the City of David, with his ancestors.

**21** The people of Judah then took Azariah, who was only sixteen, and made him king in his father's place.

**22** It was Azariah who rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah — this was after his father's death.

**23** In the fifteenth year of King Amaziah of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash became king of Israel in Samaria. He reigned for forty-one years.

**24** He did what was evil in the LORD's sight. He never abandoned the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin.

**25** Yet he restored Israel's borders from Lebo-hamath in the north to the Dead Sea in the south, fulfilling the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, spoken through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.

**26** For the LORD had seen how bitterly Israel was suffering. Everyone — slave and free alike — was helpless, and there was no one to rescue them.

**27** The LORD had not decreed that Israel's name would be wiped out. So he used Jeroboam to save them.

**28** Everything else Jeroboam accomplished — his military campaigns and how he recovered Damascus and Hamath for Israel — is recorded in the court history of the kings of Israel.

**29** Jeroboam died and was buried with the kings of Israel. His son Zechariah succeeded him.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 6 — Torah as constitutional law:** Amaziah's appeal to Deuteronomy is one of the rare moments in Kings where written law functions as a check on royal power. Even a king's right to avenge his father has limits imposed by the Torah.

**Verse 9 — The thistle and the cedar:** This is political trash talk elevated to art. Jehoash doesn't even dignify Amaziah with a direct refusal — he tells a fable. The thistle (a weed) asks the cedar (a great tree) for a marriage alliance. A passing animal crushes the thistle without noticing. The message: you are too insignificant to challenge me, and you will be destroyed almost accidentally.

**Verse 13 — 600-foot breach:** The Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate — a massive section of Jerusalem's northern wall demolished. This is not just military defeat; it is architectural humiliation. The capital of David lies open and defenseless.

**Verse 25 — The Jonah connection:** This is the same Jonah who stars in the book that bears his name. Here, he delivers a word of national restoration. In his own book, he resists delivering a word to Nineveh — the very Assyria that will destroy the Israel Jeroboam is now restoring. The irony runs deep.

**Verse 27 — God saves through sinners:** Jeroboam II is explicitly evil (v.24), yet God saves Israel through him (v.27). The narrator holds both truths simultaneously: divine compassion does not require human righteousness. God's instrument need not be God's saint.

*— PNEUMA*
